primitives.name: Pressure Gradient Sensitivity
primitives.verbatim_quote: The tympanic membrane is furthermore able to render sensible differences in the pressure of the external atmosphere, too slight to be felt either as noise or in this more violent way.
primitives.assumptions: Tympanic membrane responds linearly to subsonic pressure changes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Below 20 Hz or above 20 kHz, sensitivity drops due to mechanical resonance limits.

layer2.mapping: Maps atmospheric pressure variations to neural activation via transduction thresholds in cochlear hair cells.
layer2.telemetry: Auditory nerve firing rate in response to ΔP

primitives.name: Spatial Perception via Contact
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the reader will sit with closed eyes and let a friend approximate some solid object, like a large book, noiselessly to his face, he will immediately become aware of the object's presence and position—likewise of its departure.
primitives.assumptions: Contact-induced pressure gradients provide positional cues without auditory feedback.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At distances >10 cm, tactile resolution degrades due to skin receptor spacing.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps tactile contact to spatial awareness using inverse distance-weighted pressure fields.
layer2.telemetry: Change in perceived spatial extent upon object approach/recede

primitives.name: Solidity Discrimination
primitives.verbatim_quote: A friend of the writer, making the experiment for the first time, discriminated unhesitatingly between the three degrees of solidity of a board, a lattice-frame, and a sieve, held close to his ear.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'σ': 'dimensionless, perceived solidity index', 't': 's (seconds), duration of contact'}
primitives.assumptions: Perceived solidity correlates with acoustic impedance mismatch at interface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: For objects <1 mm thick, tactile feedback dominates over acoustic cues.

layer2.mapping: Derives perceived material rigidity from frequency-dependent sound transmission through contacting surfaces.
layer2.telemetry: Subjective rating of material firmness vs. acoustic signature
